title: Temporal Uncertainty Calibration in Sequential Neural Networks
text: Current uncertainty calibration methods often assume static or batch-level uncertainty, neglecting the dynamic nature of sequential data where uncertainty evolves over time. We propose a temporal uncertainty calibration framework that jointly learns uncertainty distributions across time steps using recurrent architectures with adaptive uncertainty propagation, where each layer's uncertainty is updated via a time-aware calibration loss that accounts for temporal dependencies. This approach is evaluated on time-series forecasting tasks using both synthetic and real-world datasets, measuring calibration via time-dependent reliability diagrams and out-of-sample prediction entropy.

title: Fast and Accurate Quality Control of PET Bottle Caps Using Image Calibration and Lightweight CNNs
text: Current product quality control in food and pharmaceutical industries requires precise, contactless inspection using machine vision, but real-time performance is often limited by long inference or training times in deep learning models. This research proposes a novel data preprocessing method that leverages prior knowledge of the optical system to calibrate images, enabling a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to efficiently classify PET bottle cap defects. The approach is evaluated by comparing prediction and training times—showing at least five-fold improvements over standard models—while maintaining equivalent accuracy on ImageNet-trained benchmarks.

title: Incorporating input uncertainty in deep regression via Errors-in-Variables models
text: Deep neural networks often ignore uncertainty in input features, which can lead to biased or overly confident predictions. This research proposes using a Bayesian framework with Errors-in-Variables modeling to explicitly account for input uncertainty, thereby decomposing predictive uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components. The approach is evaluated through simulated and real-world examples, comparing uncertainty coverage and prediction performance against standard deep regression models, with emphasis on improved reliability in known regression settings.

title: Post-stack seismic inversion using probabilistic and deep neural networks
text: Seismic inversion is a nonlinear, non-unique, and error-prone problem that traditionally relies on model-based methods, which can be unreliable. This research proposes using probabilistic neural networks (PNN) and deep feedforward neural networks (DFNN) to invert post-stack seismic data and extract porosity, gamma rays, and Lamé impedances, comparing results with model-based inversion (MBI). The performance of each method is evaluated by comparing predicted values with well-log data and through geological interpretation, such as time-slice analysis of deltaic environments, to assess geological correlation and reliability.

By applying the LiNLNet framework from Paper 1—using trainable linear-nonlinear units (LiNLUs) with parameterized nonlinearity p—to the ANN architecture used in Paper 2, we can assess and tune the layer-wise nonlinearity for coagulation prediction models. The performance would be evaluated by comparing prediction accuracy, confidence interval width, and coverage probability before and after layer-wise nonlinearity optimization, with the goal of improving both prediction precision and robustness in dosage recommendations.

Idea: Combining the GRU-ATL model from Paper 1 with the thermal modeling approach from Paper 2, this research proposes a unified framework that estimates both the state-of-charge (SOC) and core temperature of lithium-ion batteries using only surface and ambient temperature measurements. The GRU-ATL network would be trained to predict SOC and core temperature simultaneously, leveraging the nonlinear dynamics of battery behavior and the thermal coupling between surface and core temperatures. The framework would be evaluated using laboratory test data from a cylindrical 18,650 LIB cell, comparing the accuracy and robustness of the joint estimation against separate SOC and temperature predictions using first-order and second-order thermal models.

title: State of Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Battery Packs Using Improved Extreme Learning Machine with Dual Extended Kalman Filter
text: The inconsistent internal parameters and aging effects in lithium-ion battery packs degrade battery performance and pose safety risks, making accurate state of health (SOH) estimation critical. By integrating the improved extreme learning machine (ELM) model—trained on charge–discharge features to predict capacity—with the dual extended Kalman filter (DEKF) for real-time SOH and state of charge (SOC) estimation, a robust and efficient framework is proposed to estimate SOH under varying operating conditions and aging states. The performance of the combined model would be evaluated using the battery data from Paper 2’s manufacturing process, with metrics such as mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and root-mean-square error (RMSE) comparing predicted SOH against actual degradation trends, while also validating the DEKF’s accuracy in handling parameter inconsistencies.

title: State of Charge Estimation for Lithium-ion Batteries Using Set Membership Strategy with Improved Regularized Extreme Learning Machine
text: Combining the set membership strategy from Paper 1, which handles unknown but bounded external noise in state of charge estimation, with the improved regularized extreme learning machine from Paper 2, which provides accurate and computationally efficient predictions, allows for robust state of charge estimation under real-world noise conditions. The proposed approach uses the improved extreme learning machine to predict the state of charge, and then applies the set membership strategy to refine the estimate by constraining the prediction within a bounded interval or ellipsoid due to external disturbances. The performance is evaluated by comparing the midpoint or center of the set membership estimate against actual battery data in a simulation scenario, measuring accuracy and robustness under varying noise levels.

title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Fuzzy Sliding Mode Observer for Accurate State-of-Charge Estimation in Lithium-Ion Batteries
text: Current SOC estimation methods, such as the fuzzy sliding mode observer (FSMO) with grey prediction, suffer from chattering and limited accuracy under varying operating conditions. To improve estimation accuracy and robustness, this research proposes integrating a machine learning model—such as a neural network or a regression model trained on battery voltage and current data—to predict the future terminal voltage input for the grey predictor in the FSMO framework. The proposed approach uses ML to enhance the prediction accuracy of the future error, thereby refining the fuzzy gain adjustments and reducing chattering. The method would be evaluated by comparing the SOC estimation performance against conventional SMO and adaptive gain SMO methods using pulse and random discharge tests, with metrics including estimation error and convergence speed.

title: AWGLFuser: A Global–Local Feature Fusion Network with Adaptive Wavelet Filter for Lithium-Ion Battery State-of-Health Estimation
text: Accurate State-of-Health (SOH) estimation for lithium-ion batteries remains challenging due to limitations in adaptive denoising, multi-scale feature extraction, and effective fusion of global and local information in existing methods. We propose AWGLFuser, a network that combines an adaptive wavelet filter to suppress high-frequency noise and enhance key frequency-domain features, a global–local feature extraction module to capture multi-scale temporal dependencies, and a bidirectional cross-attention fusion module to enable deep interaction and effective integration of global and local features. The model is evaluated on NASA and XJTU datasets, with performance measured by MAE, MAPE, and RMSE, showing significant improvements over eight competing models through statistical validation.

title: A Hybrid Framework for Lithium-Ion Battery State-of-Health Estimation via Dynamic Local–Global Feature Fusion
text: Accurate state-of-health (SOH) estimation is critical for battery safety and reliability, but conventional data-driven methods often fail to capture both long-term degradation trends and evolving aging behaviors. We propose a hybrid deep learning framework, TCN–SE–TE, that combines a temporal convolutional network (TCN) to model local cycle-by-cycle degradation dynamics, a squeeze-and-excitation (SE) module to dynamically weight health indicators based on aging stages, and a transformer encoder (TE) to capture global temporal dependencies. The framework is evaluated using leave-one-out cross-validation on the University of Maryland CS2 battery dataset to assess its performance in estimating SOH across different degradation stages.

title: A State of Health Estimation Method for Lithium-Ion Battery Packs Using Two-Level Hierarchical Features and TCN–Transformer–SE
text: Accurate state of health (SOH) estimation is critical for battery pack reliability, but current methods often overlook degradation mechanisms at the module and cell levels. This research proposes a novel SOH estimation approach that extracts two-level hierarchical features: module-level incremental power curve length and cell-level temperature-weighted voltage inconsistency at the high-SOC knee point, both linked to fundamental degradation processes. The method uses a TCN–Transformer–SE model to fuse these features, with TCN capturing local temporal patterns and Transformer enabling global context awareness, while SE dynamically weights features based on their relevance. Performance is evaluated through aging experiments using multi-feature comparison, ablation studies, and benchmarking, with metrics including MAE, RMSE, R², and MAPE.

text: Accurate state-of-health (SOH) prediction is critical for battery management, but many methods fail under cell-to-cell variability, especially in later stages of degradation. This research proposes Ada-TL, a robust SOH prediction framework that combines a Transformer encoder to capture non-local dependencies and an LSTM regressor to model sequential degradation dynamics, with adaptive hyperparameter tuning for the number of attention heads, initial learning rate, and L2 regularization. The model is evaluated on four CS2 cells from the CALCE dataset using RMSE, MAE, and MAPE metrics, with emphasis on late-stage performance and long-horizon bias control to demonstrate improved robustness across diverse degradation trajectories.

title: Predicting ionic conductivity in solid-state electrolytes using 3D structural and potential landscape features
text: Current models struggle to accurately predict ionic conductivity in polymorphic materials with identical compositions but different crystal structures. We propose a 3D convolutional neural network that learns from both the 3D distribution of lithium ions and the spatial potential landscape encoded via Bond Valence Sum Energy. The model is evaluated by its ability to predict experimental ionic conductivities and rank material mobilities across different crystal structures with the same composition.

title: Private Model Averaging with Differential Privacy and Adaptive Noise Calibration
text: Current federated learning systems often use fixed noise levels in differential privacy, which can lead to suboptimal privacy guarantees or model degradation. We propose a dynamic noise calibration framework that adapts the amount of noise injected during model averaging based on the sensitivity of each client's contribution and the local data distribution, using a privacy-aware feedback loop. Evaluation will be conducted via synthetic and real-world datasets under varying privacy budgets, measuring both model accuracy and privacy loss using standard DP definitions, while comparing performance against fixed-noise baselines.

text: Current federated learning systems often rely on secure aggregation protocols that assume static or periodic key updates, leaving them vulnerable to long-term exposure of model gradients through side-channel attacks. text: Current federated learning methods struggle to balance privacy and recommendation utility, often sacrificing one for the other. Idea: This research combines the critical analysis of UHI mitigation strategies from Paper 1 with the spatially detailed UHI index calculation from Paper 2 by applying the GeoSOT grid method to assess UHI intensity across different climate regions. The approach evaluates how the calculated UHI indices vary with climate conditions and uses this variation to classify and prioritize mitigation strategies based on regional suitability, such as green space expansion in hot climates or material reflectivity in arid zones. The method would be evaluated by comparing the accuracy and efficiency of UHI index expression across climate zones and assessing the alignment of mitigation strategy recommendations with observed thermal patterns.

title: Assessing the Impact of Blue Space Geometry on Urban Heat Island Mitigation Using Long-Term Surface Parameter Changes
text: This study combines the temporal analysis of urban surface parameters from Paper 1 with the spatial evaluation of blue space geometry from Paper 2 to evaluate how changes in water body size, shape, and distribution over time influence urban heat island mitigation. By applying the remote sensing method to track water body indices from 2013 to 2022 in Tianjin, the study would correlate changes in water body geometry with surface temperature trends, particularly in urban canyons. The evaluation would involve comparing heat island intensity and surface temperature patterns in areas with different blue space configurations, using the findings to determine which geometries are most effective at providing evaporative cooling or nocturnal pollutant transport over time.

title: Assessing the impact of urban sprawl on roof-based heat island mitigation effectiveness in semiarid regions
text: In the Teresina–Timon conurbation area, urban sprawl has led to increased land surface temperatures and loss of green spaces, potentially reducing the effectiveness of cool and green roofs in mitigating the urban heat island effect. By applying the simulation model from Paper 1—specifically, the analysis of cool and green roof performance under different climate zones—to the LULC and LST data from Paper 2, we can evaluate how changes in land use due to urban expansion affect the energy-saving potential of different roof types. The evaluation would compare predicted building energy savings and ambient temperature reductions under current and expanded urban land use scenarios, assessing whether the increased urbanization diminishes the triple benefits of cool and green roofs.

text: This study addresses the gap in understanding how urban form influences urban heat island (UHI) intensity by integrating the building form typology analysis from Paper 1 with the heat amplification framework from Paper 2. By applying the cross-typology model developed in Paper 1 within the solar geoengineering framework of Paper 2, we evaluate how different building forms affect UHI amplification under solar geoengineering interventions such as sun-shade mirrors or surface treatments. The model would be evaluated by comparing UHI intensity and amplification rates across various building forms under different climate conditions, using the proposed heat amplification parameter to assess whether certain forms reduce UHI more effectively when combined with solar geoengineering solutions.

title: Evaluating green façade cooling efficiency in urban canyons under hot arid conditions
text: In hot arid climates like Tehran, urban canyon geometry—particularly the height-to-width (H/W) ratio—significantly influences canopy urban heat island (CUHI) intensity and outdoor thermal comfort. This study proposes to assess how green façades enhance cooling effects in urban canyons of varying H/W ratios using ENVI-met 5.1 simulations, focusing on summer conditions where thermal impacts are most pronounced. The effectiveness of green façades will be evaluated by comparing air temperature and Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) values across different canyon geometries and façade conditions.

title: Evaluating rooftop urban heat island mitigation measures in Osaka, Japan
text: Urban heat island effects exacerbate heat stress, energy demand, and health risks in cities like Osaka. This study proposes an integrated assessment framework to evaluate three rooftop measures—highly reflective roofs, green roofs, and rooftop water sprinkling—by simulating their temperature impacts using the WRF model and linking these to energy consumption and health outcomes via temperature sensitivity coefficients. The approach evaluates seasonal trade-offs and temporal dynamics, quantifying benefits in monetary terms through DALYs and cost–benefit analysis to identify the most effective and sustainable mitigation strategy.

title: Evaluating colored asphalt pavements for urban heat island mitigation and durability
text: Urban heat islands (UHI) exacerbate heat accumulation in cities due to heat-absorbing road surfaces. This study proposes using colored asphalt pavements—specifically olive green and dark maroon—by adding 5% iron oxide (yellow or red) to asphalt binders—to enhance solar reflection, reduce heat retention, and improve mechanical performance. The proposed approach evaluates the impact on rutting deformation (RD), dynamic stability (DS), durability under moisture and weather conditions, and temperature mitigation, comparing colored mixtures to conventional asphalt to assess their effectiveness in reducing UHI effects and improving pavement performance.

title: Surface Urban Heat Island Dynamics in Urban Regeneration Areas: A Multi-Temporal Remote Sensing Analysis of Istanbul, Türkiye
text: Urban regeneration often focuses on rebuilding buildings but may fail to improve local thermal conditions. This study proposes using multi-temporal Landsat data (2019–2023) to analyze changes in surface urban heat island (SUHI) patterns by deriving land surface temperature (LST), normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), and normalized difference built-up index (NDBI). The approach evaluates thermal dynamics through Pearson correlation, Getis–Ord Gi* hot spot analysis, and zonal statistics to assess how land-cover changes—such as demolition or redevelopment—affect local heat and vegetation recovery, providing a decision-support framework for climate-responsive urban planning.

title: Assessing the impacts of land use and urban morphology on surface urban heat island and thermal comfort in severe cold regions
text: In severe cold regions like Harbin, China, urban thermal environments and outdoor thermal comfort are influenced by land use/cover and urban morphology. This study proposes using Landsat imagery and structural equation modeling to analyze the relationship between urban morphological parameters, the urban thermal field variance index (UTFVI), and physiologically equivalent temperature (PET) across seasons. The approach evaluates how green space ratios and canopy cover (LAI) affect outdoor thermal comfort, using city block-level data to identify optimal urban design strategies for improving thermal comfort in cold climates.

title: Surface Urban Heat Island Variability in Cosenza, Southern Italy: The Roles of Urban Morphology, Extreme-Temperature Conditions, and Local Wind Conditions
text: Mediterranean cities like Cosenza face increasing surface urban heat island (SUHII) intensity due to complex terrain and urban development. This study proposes to analyze SUHII variability using summer ECOSTRESS Land Surface Temperature (LST) data (2018–2025) integrated with land-use, urban morphology, and meteorological data to identify how neighborhood-scale factors—such as building height, surface fraction, and imperviousness—modulate thermal contrasts. The approach evaluates SUHII across land-use types and under extreme-temperature conditions (TX90p), assessing how local wind patterns and urban form influence urban–rural thermal gradients in a valley setting.

title: Detecting Misinformation Through Temporal Pattern Anomalies in User Retweet Dynamics
text: Misinformation spreads rapidly through social media, often via coordinated retweet patterns that differ from normal user behavior. We propose a novel method that identifies anomalies in the temporal evolution of retweet sequences—such as sudden bursts, unnatural timing, or clustering—using time-series anomaly detection models trained on historical user behavior. The model would evaluate its effectiveness by measuring the accuracy of detecting misinformation outbreaks in real-time, using ground-truth labels from verified fact-checking databases and analyzing the latency between anomaly detection and user engagement spikes.

text: Current misinformation detection models rely heavily on textual content, but they often miss nuanced patterns in user behavior across platforms. This research proposes a novel framework that identifies and learns cross-platform behavioral signatures—such as post timing, engagement patterns, and network propagation dynamics—of users who spread misinformation, leveraging multimodal data from Twitter, Facebook, and Reddit. The model would be evaluated using a longitudinal dataset of verified misinformation events, measuring its ability to predict misinformation spread before it becomes widespread, using precision, recall, and early detection accuracy compared to text-only baselines.

text: Current misinformation detection models often fail to identify deepfake content embedded in social media posts that blend visual, audio, and text cues. This research proposes a multimodal consistency scoring framework that evaluates temporal and semantic coherence across audio, video, and text components to detect anomalies indicative of deepfake manipulation. The model would be trained on a dataset of real and synthetic media, evaluated using human judgment benchmarks and a novel consistency loss function that penalizes mismatched context across modalities.

title: An Effective Fake News Detection Model Using Machine Learning
text: Fake news spreads rapidly on social media and online news portals, posing a significant challenge due to limited available datasets and resources. This research proposes a machine learning-based model to distinguish fake news from legitimate content by evaluating eight different classifiers, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, SVM, Naive Bayes, and K-Nearest Neighbors. The model is evaluated based on precision, with the best performance achieved using the Support Vector Classifier (SVC), reaching a precision of 96%.

title: Gatekeeping Fake News Discourses on Mainstream Media Versus Social Media
text: This study investigates how mainstream media (MSM) and social media users frame "fake news" discourse, using computational topic modeling to analyze 8 million tweets and 1,350 news stories. It tests the hypothesis that SNS users engage in networked gatekeeping by attributing fake news claims to MSM bias, while MSM frames fake news as a result of social media spreading misinformation. The analysis evaluates the presence of a collective negative response—referred to as "networked flak"—on Twitter aimed at disciplining MSM, altering its tone, or eroding public trust in it.

title: Reaffirming Verification in Journalism Education Amid Fake News Challenges
text: In an environment where public trust in journalism is eroding due to the spread of fake news, this research proposes that journalism educators integrate core verification practices into curricula to restore confidence in journalistic integrity. By emphasizing rigorous fact-checking and transparent reporting processes, the study aims to instill in students a commitment to accuracy and accountability—foundational elements of traditional journalism. The effectiveness of this approach would be evaluated through student performance in verification tasks and their perceived confidence in journalistic practices compared to peers in traditional journalism programs.

text: The rapid spread of fake news and AI-generated deepfakes on social media poses significant risks to public trust, health, and economic stability. title: Fake news' as infrastructural uncanny
text: This research investigates how the spread of fake news functions as an infrastructural uncanny—disturbing the taken-for-granted routines of content circulation, engagement, and monetization online. The approach involves methodological interventions that map and challenge these infrastructural logics, enabling public experiments to reconfigure digital practices and their broader social, cultural, and political impacts.

title: The Information Warfare Role of Social Media: Fake News in the Russia - Ukraine War
text: This study investigates how social media platforms facilitate the spread of fake news during the Russia-Ukraine war, focusing on the rapid dissemination of unverified content across online news sites, YouTube, and Twitter. By analyzing 125 fake news items from Teyit, Dogrula, Dogruluk Payı, and Malumatfuruş, the research examines the extent to which subjective and edited content—such as montages—spreads quickly, with nearly half shared within the first week of the conflict. The study evaluates the role of official communication networks operating 24/7 in verifying or spreading false information, assessing their impact on public belief and information warfare dynamics.

title: Investigating how social approval influences perceptions and sharing behaviors of fake news about brands
text: This study examines whether the number of Likes on a fake news post about a brand affects users' perceptions of the brand and their likelihood to share the post, drawing on Paper 1’s finding that Likes amplify negative perceptions of politicians in partisan contexts. The proposed approach involves a field experiment where participants read or retweet a fictitious news story about a brand, with systematic increments of Likes appended to the retweets, and measures both changes in brand perception and sharing behavior. The study would evaluate the interaction between Likes, the political or social congruence of the brand message, and users’ decisions to share, testing whether social approval increases the spread of fake brand news and deepens negative brand perceptions.

text: This study combines the problem of fake news diffusion during crises (as in Paper 2) with the methodological framework of systematic literature review (as in Paper 1). title: Enhancing fake news detection through laypeople’s trust judgments in high-availability audiences
text: Given that the fake news audience is small and composed of highly available, disloyal users, and that laypeople can reliably distinguish low- from high-quality news sources, we propose using crowd-sourced trust judgments to identify and reduce exposure to fake news among these high-availability users. The approach would integrate laypeople’s real-time evaluations of news sources into social media algorithms, prioritizing content from trusted sources for users with high online availability. Evaluation would involve comparing exposure to fake news before and after implementing the trust-based ranking system, using visitation data from mobile and desktop platforms during politically sensitive periods.

title: Using fsQCA to explore how social media information literacy can combat olfactory misinformation in wildlife conservation
text: Under COVID-19 conditions, misinformation spreads rapidly through social media, and similarly, olfactory misinformation can misdirect wildlife foraging. This research proposes using fsQCA to examine how conservation professionals can apply social media information literacy (SMIL) as an innovation skill to detect and counteract false olfactory cues in wildlife management. The study would evaluate how SMIL factors—such as critical evaluation of digital sources and verification of sensory data—can be leveraged to improve the accuracy of foraging interventions, mirroring how SMIL combats fake news in digital contexts.

title: Meta-learned Graph-Augmented Transformer Model for Predicting Misinformation Engagement Based on Social Media News Use
text: This study proposes to apply the Graph-Augmented Transformer Ensemble (GETE) framework from Paper 1 to predict individual-level engagement with COVID-19 misinformation, as identified in Paper 2. By integrating user-news interaction graphs and linguistic features of social media content with a meta-learned ensemble, the model would dynamically weight inputs based on user characteristics such as personality and cognitive ability to predict belief and sharing intentions. The model would be evaluated on the survey data from Paper 2, measuring its ability to predict misinformation belief and sharing while accounting for personality traits and cognitive ability as moderators.

title: A Multi-Model Learning Framework for Fake News Detection on Social Media
text: Fake news spreads rapidly on social media, posing serious risks to public health and societal stability. This research proposes a multi-model learning framework that combines a Support Vector Machine, a Bidirectional LSTM, and a fine-tuned BERT model to detect fake news by integrating lexical, semantic, and contextual features through a weighted soft-voting ensemble. The approach is evaluated on three public benchmark datasets—LIAR, FakeNewsNet, and ISOT—measuring accuracy and F1-score to compare performance against individual models and existing baselines.

title: Fake News Detection Through LLM-Driven Text Augmentation Across Media and Languages
text: Fake news spreads widely across social media, headlines, and multilingual news, posing challenges for automated detection—especially in imbalanced, cross-media settings. We propose a framework using LLM-driven, feature-guided text augmentation to generate realistic, stylistically coherent synthetic samples across languages and media types while preserving meaning. The approach is evaluated across datasets using classical and transformer models (Random Forest, Logistic Regression, BERT, XLM-R), measuring improvements in minority-class recall and F1-score, while monitoring stability and performance on majority classes compared to oversampling methods.

title: A Multi-Mechanism Socio-Technical Theory of Wellness Misinformation
text: Wellness misinformation spreads widely on short-form platforms, yet current research often attributes its credibility to individual cognitive flaws. This study proposes the Algorithmic–Affective Misinformation Model (AAMM), a mid-range framework that explains how credibility emerges through the interaction of aesthetics, affect, and algorithms. Using qualitative interviews and cross-platform observations on TikTok and RED, the study identifies three mechanisms—esthetic legitimization, affective vulnerability, and algorithmic reinforcement—to show how misinformation becomes visually authoritative, emotionally resonant, and structurally normalized, with findings validated across cultural contexts.

title: Digital media literacy and fake news handling among Arab social media users
text: This study investigates the relationship between digital media literacy and the ability of Arab social media users to identify and handle fake news, particularly in the context of rapid digital transformation and increased reliance on social media for news. Using a cross-national survey of 800 young adults from Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Yemen, the research integrates digital media literacy with Cognitive Information Processing Theory to examine how media-related competencies and cognitive skills influence fake news detection. Findings will be evaluated through statistical correlations between digital media literacy, cognitive processing, and fake news handling skills, with additional analysis on the impact of social media usage intensity and demographic factors.

title: Does fact-checking COVID-19 fake news on social media correct readers’ false beliefs?
text: This study investigates whether fact-checking fake COVID-19 news on social media effectively corrects false beliefs among Chinese youths. It compares the impact of fact-checking exposure versus no exposure on belief correction, focusing on individuals who initially believed or were uncertain about the misinformation. The effectiveness of fact-checking is evaluated by examining how youth perceptions of the personal harm caused by fake news influence their receptiveness to corrections.

title: Testing inoculation effects in mobile instant messaging for misinformation countermeasures
text: Mobile instant messaging platforms like WhatsApp and Telegram are widely used to spread misinformation, yet effective countermeasures within these spaces remain unclear. This study proposes testing whether refutational-same (argument-matched) inoculation or cross-topic (cross-protection) messages influence users' perceived credibility and sharing intentions for false and true information. The effectiveness of these interventions would be evaluated through an online experiment measuring changes in credibility and sharing behavior, with analysis of moderators such as critical thinking, information literacy, and political orientation.
